critical_code_review_comments: towing.py operator_accept: atomic find_one_and_update with status='searching' AND operator_id=null → race-safe. Properly returns 409 on 2nd accept. Good.

Fallback assignment in get_request is read-triggered (lazy) — only fires when client polls. If client stops polling for 18s, fallback never fires until next GET. Acceptable since frontend polls every 3s, but worth noting (no background worker).
create_request notifies operators in best-effort try/except Exception:pass — silently swallows notification errors. Should at least log.
operator_feed has no recency filter — old 'searching' requests (e.g., abandoned, never polled by client) could clutter the feed. Consider {created_at: {$gte: now - 1h}} or auto-expire stale searches.
operator_ping & accept compute eta_minutes naïvely (hard-coded 15 / dist/30km·h) — fine for demo but a real ETA service would help.
TowingOperatorPage poll interval 4s while client polls 3s — operator may see a request up to 4s after creation; acceptable but could miss the 18s fallback window edge.

operator profile in accept payload includes 'user_id' that leaks to client GET /requests/{id} via the embedded operator object — minor PII (operator's userId exposed to client). Consider stripping before storing or before public serialization.
No endpoint for operator to cancel/release an accepted job (only client cancel). If operator misclicks accept, they cannot back out.

Frontend: operator-feed-empty and operator-offline both have data-testid but operator-feed wrapper only renders when feed has items — testid 'operator-feed' is on the wrapping div which exists whenever there are items; empty state uses 'operator-feed-empty'. Slightly inconsistent but functional.
